newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks post gains on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks post gains on foreign buying.

text.p: Thai stocks gained on Wednesday as foreigners bought into the heavily-discounted market during the afternoon session as finance and bank results exceeded expectations, traders said.
The SET Index gained 13.15 points, or 1.56 percent to end at 854.18. The SET 50 gained 1.39 points to 64.19.
Turnover increased sharply in the afternoon session driving daily turnover up to 5.12 billion baht.
"You can see from the increased volume that it was the foreigners who bought the market this afternoon," said the head of institutional sales at a major local broker.
The market reacted positively to a flurry of fourth quarter and year-end results from finance and securities firms and the banking sector, analysts said.
The afternoon session saw active trading of bank and finance stocks as the market digested earlier profit postings.
Despite generally poor earnings figures the results were not as bad as worst case scenarios, analysts said.
"I think people liked the way these firms have made some attempt to be conservative about their provisioning," said one senior trader.
Analysts said there was also some program buying by overseas investors.

"I think there were some people buying today who don't care about the results. They are more worried about government policy and the fact that they think the market is going to rise," said the institutional sales manager.
Traders said the short term outlook was positive given the market's reaction to results, and on the prospect of more foreign buying.
